source: create a advanture game where player can go for advanture into snow mountains and can lock their tent to be safe from coolness.

image_prompt.text: A worn track winding up out of the foothills into the snow, readable as the way onward
Snow-capped peaks standing over the map, pulling the player up towards the high ground
Hollows and overhangs cut into the icy rock, tucked off the main track, rewarding players who leave the path
A tent pitched at a small mountain campsite, sturdy enough to shut against the cold

layout_placement.text: The inside of the tent as a safe volume where the player is protected from the cold

notes: The tent is the one thing the prompt actually asks for and no Adventure option covers it - a shelter the player closes behind them for protection from an environmental pressure. It ships as free text with no type.
Cold as a damage-over-time pressure is a mechanic; the layout only owns the shelter it drives the player into.

open_questions.ask: Is the objective to reach a summit or a destination, or to keep surviving the cold for as long as you can?
Should the mountains read as bright storybook snow or as a bleak survival whiteout?

theme: Snowy alpine wilderness - deep snow, ice, bare rock, cold light

coverage_missing.ask: Is there a destination to reach, or is surviving the cold the whole loop?
Is this one mountainside you can cross in a minute, or a range you spend a session in?
Is there more than one campsite, or is the single tent the only safe spot on the map?

answers.ask: Is the objective to reach a summit or a destination, or to keep surviving the cold for as long as you can?
answers.answer: The objective is to adventure toward and reach a mountain summit; locking the tent provides a safe shelter from the cold along the way.

answers.ask: Should the mountains read as bright storybook snow or as a bleak survival whiteout?
answers.answer: Use a bleak survival whiteout look, fitting the dangerous cold mountain adventure.
